subject: math
cluster: Experiment with transformations in the plane
intro: Each rigid motion can be defined precisely. A translation slides every point the same distance in the same direction, defined by a vector (or by 'parallel' lines and equal segment lengths). A reflection over a line $\ell$ maps each point to the point the same distance on the other side of $\ell$, so $\ell$ is the perpendicular bisector of every segment joining a point to its image. A rotation about a point $P$ by angle $\theta$ keeps $P$ fixed and turns every other point along a circle centered at $P$ through angle $\theta$, so each point and its image are the same distance from $P$.

items.prompt: In a reflection over line $\ell$, how is $\ell$ related to the segment from a point to its image?

steps: A reflection sends each point to the mirror point across $\ell$.
The point and image are equidistant from $\ell$ and the segment joining them meets $\ell$ at a right angle.
So $\ell$ is the perpendicular bisector of that segment.
solution.answer: $\ell$ is the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining the point to its image.

items.prompt: In a rotation about point $P$, how do a point and its image relate to $P$?

steps: A rotation turns points along circles centered at $P$.
A point stays on its circle, so its distance to $P$ is unchanged.
So the point and its image are the same distance from $P$.
solution.answer: They are the same distance from $P$ (both lie on a circle centered at $P$).

items.prompt: What stays the same for every point under a single translation?

steps: A translation slides all points the same way.
Every point moves the same distance in the same direction.
So the displacement (distance and direction) is the same for every point.
solution.answer: Every point moves the same distance in the same direction.

items.prompt: What does a rotation about point $P$ keep fixed?

steps: A rotation turns the plane about its center.

items.prompt: A reflection is defined using which line relative to point-image segments?

steps: The reflection line is the mirror.
It is the perpendicular bisector of each point-to-image segment.
solution.answer: The perpendicular bisector of each point-to-image segment.

steps: A translation moves every point identically.
It is defined by a fixed distance and direction (a vector).
solution.answer: A fixed distance and direction (a translation vector).
